title: Unitree Shares Soar 629% in Shanghai Trading Debut
summary: Unitree Robotics (Yushu Technology Co. Ltd.) began trading on the Shanghai Stock Exchange's STAR Market on August 19, 2026, with shares opening at 1,100 yuan against its 150.80 yuan IPO price and soaring as much as 629% intraday, the largest first-day gain for any Shanghai listing so far this year. The offering raised about 6.1 billion yuan ($904 million), above its 4.2 billion yuan target, after retail demand oversubscribed the deal more than 8,000 times, a STAR Market record. The listing makes Unitree the first humanoid-robotics maker to go public on a mainland China exchange. Unitree reported roughly 1.7 billion yuan ($250 million) in 2025 revenue, more than 40% from overseas, though it has flagged that a July 2026 FCC ban on new foreign humanoid and quadruped robot imports could weigh on future U.S. sales; Hong Kong-listed rival UBTech fell 10.6% the same day.
whyItMatters: Unitree's Shanghai debut is the first real market test of humanoid-robotics valuations on a major exchange, giving other Chinese and global humanoid makers a public reference point as they weigh their own listings. The scale of the oversubscription and the size of the first-day pop show how much investor enthusiasm has built around embodied AI, even as analysts caution that most humanoid robots today are still used mainly for demonstrations and research rather than reliable, revenue-generating deployment.
